## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components, combined with parallel dispatch, can approach the streaming ceiling on workloads with moderate death rates.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill at N≈949 falls below the smallest measured point (N=4000), so its effect is not directly observed. Across all death rates, ns/particle FALLS from N=4000 to N=65000 — at q=0.01 from 10.009 to 8.078 ns/p — reflecting fixed-overhead amortization. The L2→DRAM spill at N≈60787 produces no knee: cost stays FLAT from N=65000 through N=4000000 (8.058–8.078 ns/p at q=0.01). Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.25 lifts the large-N plateau to ~10.2 ns/p versus ~8.0 at q=0.01, but the fall-then-flat N-shape is preserved at every q.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.73 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 34.6% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead/compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound: it never crosses 35% of ceiling at any N or death rate. Bandwidth is highest at q=0.01 (~8.5–8.7 GB/s for N≥65000) and degrades with churn — q=0.25 holds at ~6.75 GB/s for N≥262000 — because the 37 `bl` calls to `Data.spawn` per step dominate as death rate rises. No regime approaches the streaming ceiling.

## Assembly
The compiler did not auto-vectorize the particle math. The inner loop (0x100055460–0x100055680) uses scalar single-precision registers: `ldp s5, s6`, `ldp s7, s16`, `ldr s17`, `fadd s5`, `fmul s5`, `fsub s5`, `fcvtzs`. The scatter is entirely scalar byte-granular: 45 `ldrb` and 16 `strb` with `csel` clamping per RGB channel. The only vector code is a mask-skip fast path (0x1000556c8) using `ldp q1, q0`, `orr.16b`, `ext.16b`, `orr.8b` to OR-reduce 32 mask bytes and skip chunks with no spawns — vectorization across mask bytes, not across particle components. The histogram reports 0 vector-suffixed instructions, consistent with no `.4s`/`.2s` float SIMD. Scalar byte scatter and 37 function-call sites explain why bandwidth stalls at 35% of ceiling: the workload is instruction-bound, not memory-bound.

## Verdict
Refuted — the compiler emitted no auto-vectorized particle math (scalar `s`-register FP, scalar `ldrb`/`strb` scatter), and peak bandwidth reaches only 8.73 GB/s = 35% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling at q=0.01, N=262000. At q=0.25 the 37 `bl` spawn calls per step drop throughput to 6.75 GB/s (27% of ceiling). The hypothesis that auto-vectorization approaches the streaming ceiling does not hold in any measured regime.
